scope: Current frozen Alden narration claims compared with freshly read primary text. Script support is separate from the completed movie’s factual/mechanical/continuous/listening review; no output review or pilot acceptance is granted. No manufacturing dimensions or simulated force results are inferred.

episodes.question: Why does the hook on a tape measure move?
episodes.claimSummary: Hook travel compensates for its own thickness when changing contact face.
episodes.designBoundary: Outside pull uses the inner hook face; inside push uses the outer face. The model thickness is conceptual.

support.title: Why does the hook on the end of the Stanley tape rule move?
support.locator: Explanation of hook thickness and inside/outside measurement

renderedWitnessesRequired: Confirm visible selected faces and equal hook-thickness travel throughout the completed movie.

episodes.question: Why does a cable tie tighten but resist pulling backward?
episodes.selectedDesign: one-piece outside-serrated nylon cable tie with integral rooted plastic tongue
episodes.claimSummary: An integral flexible tongue passes strap teeth forward and engages them against backward withdrawal.
episodes.designBoundary: Applies to the selected one-piece serrated nylon construction, not every cable-tie locking system.

support.title: Cable ties and zip ties for industry
support.locator: FAQ: How does a cable tie fastener work?; Cable ties with plastic pawls

renderedWitnessesRequired: Confirm tongue deflection/recovery and reverse retaining contact at the spoken phases.

episodes.claimSummary: Closing the handle ends overcomes the central spring and opens the gripping ends; the spring tends to close them after release.
episodes.designBoundary: Use conventional members64/65 and spring66. Fig7 depicts a failure state; improved retaining clips and pins are excluded.

support.title: Clothespin
support.locator: Conventional Fig7 description, members64/65, tails69/71, coil76 and ends77/78

explicitInferences: Continued load with fabric between the jaws is an inference from the spring closing tendency and prevented full closure, not a measured force result.

support.title: To begin with, what’s the structure of a zipper?

episodes.question: How does a keyhole mounting slot hold a screw?
episodes.selectedDesign: Conventional keyhole slot disclosed in EP1817988A1 background: enlarged entry then narrower shank track, without the invention’s additional snap neck.
episodes.claimSummary: The enlarged opening admits a fastener head; the narrow portion accepts its shank while surrounding material retains the wider head.
episodes.designBoundary: The selected conventional slot excludes the patent invention’s additional snap neck. Reverse translation can disengage it.

support.title: Picture frame fixings
support.locator: Opening description of known keyhole fixings, before the snap-fit invention

episodes.question: Why do binder-clip handles make the jaws open?
episodes.selectedDesign: US1139627A continuous triangular sheet-steel binder, integral rolled jaw journals and body-bearing wire levers; authored U-handle proportions, clamping action only
episodes.claimSummary: The clip’s spring-steel body provides closing force; the wire handles use the body/back as a fulcrum to spread its jaws.
episodes.designBoundary: Covers the selected clamping operation. The patent also uses resilient handles for retention and folding; the narration does not deny that elasticity.

support.title: Paper-binding clip
support.locator: Opening description; bodyA/B, tubular jaws1/2 and handleD operation in Figs1–3

explicitInferences: Persistent grip with paper preventing full closure follows from the documented resilient body; no measured force or stiffness is claimed.
renderedWitnessesRequired: Confirm handle/body bearing and jaw opening, continuous body deformation and paper-held return.
